content.title: About
content.content: Kidney beans with meat is a classic stew where large red beans are cooked together with chunks of beef or pork in a savory tomato‑based sauce. The beans provide plant protein and fiber, while the meat adds a rich flavor and an additional source of animal protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red kidney beans are called “kidney beans” because of their kidney‑shaped appearance.
The dish is popular in American, Mexican and Russian home cooking.
Beans must be soaked for at least 8 hours and boiled before cooking to destroy the toxin phytohaemagglutinin.
Traditional seasonings include bay leaf, paprika, cumin and garlic.
It is often served with rice, mashed potatoes or fresh bread.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The combination of beans and meat supplies a complete set of essential amino acids important for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from the beans supports digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat and beans together improve iron bioavailability, which is valuable for preventing anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The stew provides thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Beneficial minerals
items.content: Magnesium, potassium and phosphorus are present, supporting heart function and bone health.

items.title: Toxin in raw beans
items.content: Raw red kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin, a toxin destroyed only by thorough boiling; always pre‑cook beans before stewing.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made broth or soy sauce can make the dish overly salty; monitor added salt.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Digestive load
items.content: Large amounts of beans can cause gas and discomfort in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak the beans for 8–12 hours, then boil for 10‑15 minutes. Brown the meat pieces, add onion, carrot, garlic, spices and tomato paste. Pour in broth, add the beans and simmer on low heat for 45‑60 minutes until tender. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked stew in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, portion into containers and freeze for up to 2‑3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat thoroughly before serving.
